exposure: Mode of vaginal birth (spontaneous vs. vacuum-assisted)
Type of vacuum cup (Kiwi Omnicup vs. Bird's anterior metal cup)
outcome: Incidence and distribution of different tear types
cohort: Nulliparous and multiparous women with a singleton pregnancy in vertex presentation at ≥37 + 0 gestational weeks who gave birth vaginally at a tertiary care center between June 2012 and December 2016
finding: There were more episiotomies, vaginal tears, and OASIS after vacuum-assisted vaginal birth than after spontaneous birth, while more low-grade perineal and labial tears were observed after spontaneous birth.
mod_finding: No significant differences were found in tear distribution between the Kiwi Omnicup and Bird's anterior metal cup vacuum systems.
